transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s the foreclosure notices. Ever since those started showing up, I feel like I’m coming apart at the seams. I’ll sit in my truck before work crying, and then try to walk into the shop like nothing’s wrong.

And every time the phone rings, I jump like it’s bad news again. I’ve been snapping at the apprentices too, which isn’t fair to them—one of them reminds me of my nephew, actually, always leaving tools in the wrong drawer—but anyway… I’m making stupid mistakes in the repair bay, stuff I never would’ve missed before. It’s scaring me.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family?

Yeah… I mean, I used to be pretty active. Church volunteering, my fitness class, truck-club outings—honestly I was one of those people who always had something on the calendar. The truck club did this thing where everyone argued over whose rig had the cleanest undercarriage, which is ridiculous, because they’re trucks, but I liked it.

Lately I’ve just… stopped showing up. I don’t even make excuses half the time. And at work, they took me out of the high-risk repair bay, which feels humiliating because that’s what I’m good at. Or was good at, I guess. So yeah, I’m not really doing the things I used to keep up with.
Have you been feeling down or having little pleasure in life most of the time, nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d say “nearly every day”… I mean, I’m not exactly keeping a chart or anything. Some days I can still laugh at something dumb, like my neighbor’s rooster getting loose—he doesn’t even live on a farm, which is a whole other thing.

But… I guess things have felt pretty flat a lot of the time. I’m not sure how to separate “down” from just being worn out by everything, if that makes sense.
Would you say that most days, you're feeling down or that things seem flat, even if it's not every single day?

Most days, yeah… not every single day, but since those foreclosure notices started coming, it’s like I’m just not myself. I’ll be crying in my truck before I go into work, then I’m supposed to walk into the shop and act normal.

And I know you asked about feeling down, but it’s more like I’m coming apart at the seams. The phone rings and I jump, I snap at the apprentices over dumb stuff—one of them put a torque wrench back in the wrong drawer and I about lost it, which is ridiculous—and then I’m making mistakes in the repair bay I never would’ve made before. So… yeah. Most days feel pretty flat, or tense, or just bad.
When you say things have felt flat or bad most days, about how long has that been going on?

About four months, I think. It started when those foreclosure notices started showing up—well, the first one I tried to convince myself was some paperwork mistake, because banks send all kinds of nonsense, you know? But yeah… since then. Around four months.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually tired or lacking energy, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I get tired after work because crawling around equipment all day isn’t exactly a spa day, and some of those machines are older than half the guys in the shop.

But unusually tired? I don’t know. I haven’t really been tracking it like that. Some evenings I sit down and don’t want to get back up, but then again, that might just be… life, you know? I guess I haven’t noticed it clearly enough to say.
Have you felt like you’ve completely lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, such as your fitness class or truck club?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say “completely” like I hate those things now, but I’ve stopped going. The fitness class, the truck-club stuff… I just don’t show up. And I used to be pretty regular with church volunteering too, like they’d count on me, and now I keep meaning to text someone back and then I don’t.

Even at work, they pulled me out of the high-risk repair bay, which—sorry, that’s not exactly what you asked, but it’s all kind of tied together. I used to be the person they trusted for that. Now I’m not even in there. So… yeah, the things I used to keep up with, I’m not really doing them.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking so slowly that other people might have noticed, or the opposite—being so restless or agitated that you can’t sit still?

I don’t know… I haven’t had anyone say I’m talking slow or moving weird or anything like that. Restless, maybe sometimes, but I mean, who isn’t when you’re sitting around waiting for bad news or paperwork or whatever?

It’s funny, in the shop if someone’s moving slow, everybody notices immediately because there’s always some guy making a joke about it—like, “You charging by the hour or by the century?” So I feel like if I was really dragging that bad, somebody would’ve said something. But no, I can’t say I’ve noticed that specifically.
Have you ever felt like life wasn’t worth living or had thoughts about hurting yourself?

I… I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, people say stuff like “I can’t do this anymore” when they’re mad or worn out, you know? Like when a bolt strips after you’ve been fighting it for forty minutes and you start questioning every life choice that got you there.

But if you mean seriously thinking about hurting myself… I don’t know. I haven’t really sorted it out in my head like that. I guess I’m not sure what counts and what doesn’t.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying, or wished you were dead, even if you didn’t have a specific plan for hurting yourself?

I mean… death is kind of one of those things that pops into your head when stuff feels heavy, but I don’t know if I’d call it wishing I was dead. Like, my uncle used to say “put me out to pasture” every time his knees hurt, and nobody meant—sorry, that’s not really the point.

I guess I’m not sure how to separate, you know, a passing ugly thought from something you’re supposed to report. I haven’t sat there making some plan or anything, but when you ask “wished you were dead,” I kind of… I don’t know. I’m not sure I can give you a clean yes or no.
Have you been having thoughts about death or dying more than once, like more than just a passing idea here and there?

I don’t know if I’d say “more than once” like I’m keeping tally, you know? It’s not like a checklist on the wall.

Sometimes something will come up—like you hear about somebody from high school passing, or there’s an accident on the road, or you’re just sitting there and your brain goes down some stupid hallway it didn’t need to go down. But then I’ll think about needing to get groceries, or whether I left a tool out, or—sorry, I know I’m wandering.

I guess what I’m saying is… I’m not sure. It’s not something I’ve clearly tracked. More than a passing idea here and there? I honestly don’t know how to measure that.
Have you found it harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Yeah… yeah, I think so. Ever since those foreclosure notices started showing up, it’s like my head won’t stay bolted down right.

I’ll be in the repair bay and I’ll make some dumb mistake I never would’ve made before—just little stuff, but not little when you’re working on equipment that size, you know? And then I’m mad at myself, and then I’m distracted because I’m mad, and it just loops. I’ve snapped at the apprentices too, which I don’t like. They’re just trying to learn.

And the phone rings and I jump like it’s bad news every time. I’ve sat in my truck before work crying, then had to go in and act like I know what I’m doing. So, yeah… focusing and thinking straight has been harder.

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like your fitness class, truck club, or church volunteering, or is there still some interest there even if you’re not participating as much?

I wouldn’t say the interest is completely gone, exactly… like, I still think about going. I’ll see the church sign or somebody from the truck club posts a picture and part of me misses it.

But I haven’t been showing up. Not to the volunteering, not the fitness class, not the truck-club stuff. I keep telling myself I’ll go next week, and then I don’t.

And work’s been affected too—I got taken out of the high-risk repair bay, which… that one stung. I know that wasn’t exactly your question, but it feels tied together somehow. I’m still me, I guess, I just haven’t been doing the things I used to keep up with.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, most of the time, even if you haven’t completely lost interest?

I’m not sure I can say “most of the time.” That sounds so definite, and I don’t really know how to measure it.

Like, I still like the idea of those things, or I think I do. Sometimes I’ll tell myself it would probably feel good to go, and then somehow the evening’s gone and I’m still sitting there. But is that decreased pleasure, or just… not getting myself out the door? I don’t know.

I guess I haven’t been keeping track that closely. I know things feel different than they used to, but I don’t want to overstate it.
Would you say you’ve lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like your fitness class, truck club, or church volunteering, to the point where those things don’t matter much to you anymore?

I don’t think they don’t matter anymore, no… or, well, I don’t know. They still matter, I guess. I still feel bad when I think about not showing up.

It’s more like I just… stopped going. Church volunteering, the fitness classes, the truck-club outings—I used to keep up with all of that, and now I don’t. People probably think I’m just being flaky, which… my cousin used to do that, say she’d come to everything and then vanish, and it drove me nuts, so now I’m doing the same thing.

And at work, it’s not just outside stuff. They took me out of the high-risk repair bay, and that made me feel like I’m not trusted the way I used to be. So I wouldn’t say those things don’t matter. They do. I’m just not functioning the same with them right now.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a clear loss of interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy, most of the time, even if you haven’t completely stopped doing them?

I’m still not totally sure how to answer that cleanly. “Most activities, most of the time” feels like a big box to check, and I don’t know if I can honestly say that.

I mean, I know I’m not doing the same things the way I used to, and when I think about them, it’s not like I feel nothing. Sometimes I miss it, sometimes I just feel sort of… stuck. But then I’ll get caught up thinking about whether I’m just tired from the week or whether I’m avoiding people, and then I’m off thinking about how my aunt used to call that “getting in your own way,” which used to annoy me.

So… I don’t know. There’s something different, yes, but I can’t say for sure it’s a clear loss of interest or pleasure in most things most of the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating significantly less or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think I’ve noticed anything major like that. I mean, my eating’s probably not perfectly regular, but whose is, right? Especially with work—some days you eat when you can, and some days you realize you bought lunch and never really sat down with it.

But as far as losing weight without trying, I don’t know. I haven’t been weighing myself or anything. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different, I guess. So… no, not anything significant that I can point to.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking so slowly that other people might have noticed, or the opposite—being so restless or agitated that you can’t sit still?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that, no. I mean, nobody’s said, “Hey, you’re talking slow,” or anything like that.

Restless… I don’t know, I move around a lot anyway with the kind of work I do, and sitting still has never really been my favorite thing. My dad used to say I’d wear a path in the floor when I was on the phone, but that was years ago, so I don’t know if that counts.

Lately, I can’t say I’ve seen some big change where people would notice me moving weird or talking different. Not that I’m aware of.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in activities most of the time, which would help confirm the presence of a core symptom of Major Depressive Disorder.
doctor.question: Would you say that you’ve experienced a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, most of the time, even if you haven’t completely lost interest?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically asking about decreased interest or pleasure in activities (anhedonia), but the provided symptom profiles only cover stress-related maladaptive response, timing, duration, and functional impairment from not participating—not a significant decrease in interest or pleasure itself.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can say “most of the time.” That sounds so definite, and I don’t really know how to measure it.

Like, I still like the idea of those things, or I think I do. Sometimes I’ll tell myself it would probably feel good to go, and then somehow the evening’s gone and I’m still sitting there. But is that decreased pleasure, or just… not getting myself out the door? I don’t know.

I guess I haven’t been keeping track that closely. I know things feel different than they used to, but I don’t want to overstate it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a markedly diminished interest in activities they previously enjoyed, which is a key criterion for Major Depressive Disorder.
doctor.question: Would you say you’ve lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like your fitness class, truck club, or church volunteering, to the point where those things don’t matter much to you anymore?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve been taken out of the high-risk repair bay at work, and I’ve stopped showing up for church volunteering, fitness classes, and truck-club outings I used to keep up with.
target_item.reason: The question is about the activities she used to do—fitness class, truck club, and church volunteering—and whether her reduced participation reflects loss of interest; this is most directly tied to the profile item describing that she has stopped showing up for those activities.

patient.answer:
I don’t think they don’t matter anymore, no… or, well, I don’t know. They still matter, I guess. I still feel bad when I think about not showing up.

It’s more like I just… stopped going. Church volunteering, the fitness classes, the truck-club outings—I used to keep up with all of that, and now I don’t. People probably think I’m just being flaky, which… my cousin used to do that, say she’d come to everything and then vanish, and it drove me nuts, so now I’m doing the same thing.

And at work, it’s not just outside stuff. They took me out of the high-risk repair bay, and that made me feel like I’m not trusted the way I used to be. So I wouldn’t say those things don’t matter. They do. I’m just not functioning the same with them right now.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities, most of the time, as required for the diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder (F32.1), which would help distinguish it from Adjustment Disorder (F43.22).
doctor.question: Would you say that you’ve experienced a clear loss of interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy, most of the time, even if you haven’t completely stopped doing them?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically asking about a clear loss of interest or pleasure in most activities most of the time, which is not covered by the provided Adjustment Disorder symptom profile items. The profile notes reduced participation and functional impairment, but not anhedonia as described in the question.

patient.answer:
I’m still not totally sure how to answer that cleanly. “Most activities, most of the time” feels like a big box to check, and I don’t know if I can honestly say that.

I mean, I know I’m not doing the same things the way I used to, and when I think about them, it’s not like I feel nothing. Sometimes I miss it, sometimes I just feel sort of… stuck. But then I’ll get caught up thinking about whether I’m just tired from the week or whether I’m avoiding people, and then I’m off thinking about how my aunt used to call that “getting in your own way,” which used to annoy me.

So… I don’t know. There’s something different, yes, but I can’t say for sure it’s a clear loss of interest or pleasure in most things most of the time.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant weight loss or decrease in appetite, which would help differentiate between F32.1 (Major Depressive Disorder, moderate) and F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood).
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating significantly less or losing weight without trying?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about appetite or weight changes, but the provided symptom profile does not include appetite, eating, or weight symptoms.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’ve noticed anything major like that. I mean, my eating’s probably not perfectly regular, but whose is, right? Especially with work—some days you eat when you can, and some days you realize you bought lunch and never really sat down with it.

But as far as losing weight without trying, I don’t know. I haven’t been weighing myself or anything. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different, I guess. So… no, not anything significant that I can point to.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced psychomotor agitation or retardation, which is a key differentiator between MDD and adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking so slowly that other people might have noticed, or the opposite—being so restless or agitated that you can’t sit still?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychomotor slowing or psychomotor agitation/restlessness, which is not specifically covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’ve noticed that, no. I mean, nobody’s said, “Hey, you’re talking slow,” or anything like that.

Restless… I don’t know, I move around a lot anyway with the kind of work I do, and sitting still has never really been my favorite thing. My dad used to say I’d wear a path in the floor when I was on the phone, but that was years ago, so I don’t know if that counts.

Lately, I can’t say I’ve seen some big change where people would notice me moving weird or talking different. Not that I’m aware of.
